edges.description: Loss of RECQL4 helicase function impairs DNA replication and DNA repair, since RECQL4 participates in both processes.
RECQL4-deficient cells accumulate a senescent phenotype, which the authors of the CRIPT report propose as the mechanism shared with the other RTS genes.
Defective replication and repair lead to accumulation of DNA damage and chromosomal instability.

Juvenile cataracts segregate with the ANAPC1-related form rather than with the RECQL4-related one. The steps between reduced APC/C activity and lens opacity are not established, so this edge records the genotype-phenotype association the sources report rather than a worked mechanism.
Accumulated genomic instability in mesenchymal/osteoblastic lineages drives osteosarcoma, the hallmark malignancy of RTS type 2.
The predisposition is realized as osteosarcoma in roughly a third of patients in the reference clinical cohort.
CRIPT-deficient fibroblasts carry a senescent phenotype, which is the cellular consequence the originating report measured.
Neurodevelopmental delay accompanies the RTS features in every reported CRIPT individual. No intermediate mechanism has been established.
Seizures accompany the RTS features in the reported CRIPT individuals. No intermediate mechanism has been established.

The originating report proposes the shared senescent phenotype as the mechanism behind the clinical features that RECQL4- and CRIPT-related disease have in common, of which poikiloderma is the hallmark. The intermediate steps are not established.
Reduced DNA2 protein leaves double-strand break repair impaired, which is the same node the RECQL4 lesion feeds.
Severe short stature is part of the presenting triad in every reported individual with this genotype. The intermediate steps are not established.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ANAPC1, Encoding a Scaffold Subunit of the Anaphase-Promoting Complex, Cause Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome Type 1.
evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate that deficiency in the APC/C is a cause of RTS type 1

nodes.description: Biallelic ANAPC1 mutations reduce levels of a scaffold subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C). A deep intronic splicing mutation activates a 95 bp pseudoexon, producing transcripts with premature termination codons subject to nonsense-mediated decay, decreased ANAPC1 protein, and prolongation of interphase. APC/C deficiency causes RTS type 1 and is associated with juvenile cataracts.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ANAPC1, Encoding a Scaffold Subunit of the Anaphase-Promoting Complex, Cause Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome Type 1.
evidence.snippet: identified a deep intronic splicing mutation of the ANAPC1 gene, a component of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), in all affected individuals

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ANAPC1, Encoding a Scaffold Subunit of the Anaphase-Promoting Complex, Cause Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome Type 1.
evidence.snippet: the intronic mutation causes the activation of a 95 bp pseudoexon, leading to mRNAs with premature termination codons and nonsense-mediated decay, decreased ANAPC1 protein levels, and prolongation of interphase

nodes.description: Biallelic CRIPT variants remove the protein HGNC names as the CXXC repeat containing interactor of PDZ3 domain. Affected individuals meet the RTS diagnostic criteria and, unlike the other three molecular forms, also have neurodevelopmental delay and seizures. The route from CRIPT loss to those neurological features is not established.

evidence.snippet: Thus, we have broadened the phenotypical spectrum of DNA2 mutations, incorporating clinical characteristics of RTS.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic variants in DNA2 cause poikiloderma with congenital cataracts and severe growth failure reminiscent of Rothmund-Thomson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Although a clear genotype-phenotype correlation cannot be definitively established at this moment, we speculate that the residual activity of the splicing variant allele could be responsible for the distinct manifestations of DNA2-related syndromes.

nodes.description: A shared deep intronic splicing variant in trans with a loss-of-function allele reduces DNA2 protein levels in the reported cohort, and patient cells show impaired DNA double-strand break repair. The same gene causes microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism, and the sources state that the genotype-phenotype correlation separating the two DNA2 syndromes is not yet established.

nodes.description: Cells from RTS patients show genomic instability often associated with chromosomal rearrangements that cause acquired somatic mosaicism. This instability is the proximate driver of the cancer predisposition, particularly osteosarcoma, that characterizes RTS type 2.

biological_processes: double-strand break repair via homologous recombination

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in RECQL4 cause a subset of cases of Rothmund-Thomson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Cytogenetic studies indicate that cells from affected patients show genomic instability often associated with chromosomal rearrangements causing an acquired somatic mosaicism.

nodes.description: RECQL4 deficiency compromises DNA replication and repair. Both RECQL4 and the APC/C (deficient in RTS type 1) are involved in DNA repair and replication, providing a possible mechanistic link between the two RTS types.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ANAPC1, Encoding a Scaffold Subunit of the Anaphase-Promoting Complex, Cause Rothmund-Thomson Syndrome Type 1.

nodes.description: Juvenile (early-onset) cataracts are characteristic of RTS and are particularly associated with type 1 (ANAPC1-related) disease. Mice heterozygous for an ANAPC1 knockout show an increased incidence of cataracts.

nodes.description: Neurodevelopmental delay, with speech particularly affected, accompanies the RTS features in individuals with biallelic CRIPT variants and is one of the two findings that separate the CRIPT-related subtype from the other three.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic variants in CRIPT cause a Rothmund-Thomson-like syndrome with increased cellular senescence.
evidence.snippet: All CRIPT individuals fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for RTS and additionally had neurodevelopmental delay and seizures.

nodes.description: RTS confers a markedly increased risk of osteosarcoma, the hallmark malignancy of type 2 (RECQL4) disease. In a cohort of 41 patients, 32% had osteosarcoma; osteosarcoma risk is associated with truncating RECQL4 mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical manifestations in a cohort of 41 Rothmund-Thomson syndrome patients.
evidence.snippet: Thirteen subjects had osteosarcoma (OS) (32%)

evidence.reference_title: Association between osteosarcoma and deleterious mutations in the RECQL4 gene in Rothmund-Thomson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Rothmund-Thomson syndrome (RTS) is an autosomal recessive disorder associated with an increased predisposition to osteosarcoma.

nodes.description: RTS, especially type 2 with truncating RECQL4 mutations, carries a markedly increased risk of osteosarcoma. Osteosarcoma incidence is essentially zero in truncating-mutation-negative patients but elevated in those carrying truncating RECQL4 mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Association between osteosarcoma and deleterious mutations in the RECQL4 gene in Rothmund-Thomson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Mutations predicted to result in the loss of RECQL4 protein function occurred in approximately two-thirds of RTS patients and are associated with risk of osteosarcoma.

nodes.description: A rash that develops in infancy (typically ages three to six months) as erythema, swelling, and blistering on the face, subsequently spreading to the buttocks and extremities, then evolving over months to years into chronic reticulated hypo- and hyperpigmentation, telangiectasias, and punctate atrophy (collectively, poikiloderma) that persists throughout life. It is the cardinal and near-universal feature of RTS.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical manifestations in a cohort of 41 Rothmund-Thomson syndrome patients.
evidence.snippet: All subjects displayed a characteristic rash.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from individuals with either RECQL4 or CRIPT variants show raised senescence markers and raised senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity. The same study found these cells were not unusually sensitive to genotoxic stress, so for CRIPT the senescent phenotype is reported without an accompanying measurable DNA-repair defect, and the authors offer senescence rather than genome instability as the mechanism the RTS genes share.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic variants in CRIPT cause a Rothmund-Thomson-like syndrome with increased cellular senescence.
evidence.snippet: Skin biopsies revealed a high expression of senescence markers (p53/p16/p21) and the senescence-associated ß-galactosidase activity was elevated in CRIPT-deficient fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic variants in CRIPT cause a Rothmund-Thomson-like syndrome with increased cellular senescence.
evidence.snippet: RECQL4- and CRIPT-deficient fibroblasts showed an unremarkable mitotic progression and unremarkable number of mitotic errors and no or only mild sensitivity to genotoxic stress by ionizing radiation, mitomycin C, hydroxyurea, etoposide, and potassium bromate.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in RECQL4 cause a subset of cases of Rothmund-Thomson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: mutation of RECQL4 at human chromosome 8q24.3 is responsible for at least some cases of RTS

evidence.reference_title: Association between osteosarcoma and deleterious mutations in the RECQL4 gene in Rothmund-Thomson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Twenty-three RTS patients, including all 11 osteosarcoma patients, carried at least one of 19 truncating mutations in their RECQL4 genes.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in RECQL4 cause loss of a RecQ-family DNA helicase that unwinds double-stranded DNA into single strands. RECQL4 is one of the human RecQ helicases (alongside WRN and BLM, mutated in Werner and Bloom syndromes) and functions in DNA replication and repair. Its deficiency underlies RTS type 2.
